players.product: Turnkey HPC data-center campuses leased to hyperscalers (Barber Lake, Black Pearl, Stingray - Texas) - ex-Bitcoin-mining, now 'Cipher Digital'

quarterly_data.signal: Our three executed data center campus leases are expected to generate approximately $793 million of average annualized net operating income from October 2026 through September 2036 - stable, visible, and contracted net operating income from long-term agreements with investment-grade counterparties. Three data center campuses leased to some of the most sophisticated technology companies in the world, representing billions of dollars of contracted revenue locked in over the next decade plus.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$793M average annualized NOI, October 2026 through September 2036, from 3 leases

quarterly_data.signal: Black Pearl: at the request of our tenant, we executed an amendment to the lease that accelerated the development timeline of initial capacity. The first data center capacity at Black Pearl was delivered in August, two full months ahead of the original schedule, and rent has commenced at the site. We've secured approximately 96% of the equipment required across both phase I and phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: First Black Pearl capacity delivered 2 months early, rent commenced; 96% of phase I+II equipment secured

quarterly_data.signal: Barber Lake phase I, comprising approximately 168 critical IT megawatts, remains on track with rental payments expected to commence in October. Our tenant has commenced beneficial use of the facility, including partial occupancy of the building and deployment of network racks. We've also now secured 100% of the equipment required to complete the project; first phase of data center capacity to be delivered in September.
quarterly_data.figure: ~168 critical IT MW; delivery September, rent from October 2026; 100% of equipment secured

quarterly_data.signal: Stingray: we priced an $810 million bond offering at a 6% coupon, fully funding Stingray through substantial completion - our third project-level bond issuance, priced tighter than our previous bonds despite spreads widening, approximately 8x oversubscribed. With approximately 75% of the equipment secured, expected delivery in the first half of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: $810M project notes at 6% coupon; 75% of equipment secured; delivery 1H 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Across our operating, contracted, and future pipeline developments, the portfolio now totals approximately 5.3 GW of capacity spread across 11 sites. On the operating and contracted side, we remain at 907 MW. We expect Reveille and Ulysses to add 270 gross megawatts in 2027; Colchis, Mikeska, and McLennan another 2 GW in 2028 and 2029; Milsing, Apollo and expansions at Barber Lake and Stingray up to an additional 2.1 GW in 2030 and beyond. Pipeline of approximately 4.4 GW of expected future developments.
quarterly_data.figure: ~5.3 GW across 11 sites; 907 MW operating+contracted; ~4.4 GW future pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: This quarter, we added up to 1.1 GW of potential new future capacity in Texas with a new 900 MW site called Apollo (option; up to 900 MW by 2031, within 25 mi of San Antonio, submitted as a studied load in Batch Zero) and a planned 200 MW expansion at our current Stingray site. The 500 MW Barber Lake expansion is expected to be in Batch Zero.
quarterly_data.figure: Apollo 900 MW option + Stingray 200 MW expansion = up to 1.1 GW added; Barber Lake 500 MW expansion

quarterly_data.signal: Cipher has 477 MW potentially available in 2027 outside of the ERCOT batch process (Odessa 207 MW - currently 11.6 exahash of Bitcoin mining under a fixed-price PPA with Vistra Luminant running through end of July 2027; Reveille and Ulysses fully interconnection approved). All of those are past whatever milestones they would need to get a lease; we are in discussions with multiple potential tenants. I have never seen a better environment for us in terms of how lease terms are evolving with higher rents, longer time periods, triple net structures.
quarterly_data.figure: 477 MW leasable in 2027 outside Batch Zero (Odessa 207 MW HPC conversion target end-2027)

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue for the second quarter was $25 million, down from $35 million in Q1, reflecting the decommissioning of Bitcoin mining at Black Pearl, in line with our transition toward contracted data center revenue. GAAP net loss of $268 million, driven by a $150.5 million non-cash warrant remeasurement loss.

In Q2, we spent about $400 million in CapEx. About $50 million of that was on the development pipeline. Construction in progress grew $1.4 billion-$1.68 billion, reflecting the simultaneous construction ramp at Barber Lake, Black Pearl and Stingray. Restricted project cash totaled approximately $3.7 billion, including approximately $3.2 billion reserved for construction; total unrestricted liquidity $870 million. We do not expect to require additional equity for the sites right in front of us.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex ~$400M (~$50M on development pipeline); ~$3.2B restricted construction cash; $870M unrestricted liquidity

quarterly_data.signal: Build-cost inflation: we definitely see inflation on labor and equipment across the board. As we build budgets for the next build, I would expect our budgeting to go up, and that probably translates into a higher cost per megawatt (analyst-cited historical range $9 million-$11 million per megawatt). We're running at the contingency level given that inflation. At some of our sites we put a cap on the CapEx that we have exposure to and pass this risk to the tenant.
quarterly_data.figure: cost per MW expected to creep higher from the $9M-$11M/MW range; running at contingency level
